To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the aggregation and toxicity of the Alzheimer's beta-amyloid protein is dependent upon the time the protein is allowed to aggregate.

(1) the neurotoxicity and fibrillization of beta amyloid (beta A), a peptide implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease, are time-dependent phenomena, and (2) the neurotoxicty of beta A1–40 is related to its fibrillar state.

the aggregation of beta-amyloids in solution is a time-dependent process, which can be accelerated by the addition of certain chemicals, such as copper, and that the neurotoxicity associated with these aggregates depends upon their conformational state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a cell based assay for the detection of neurotoxic peptides and with the development of an infra-red based assay for the quantification of beta-amyloids.
the development of neurodegenerative disease, in particular Alzheimer's disease.
the study of the neurotoxicity and aggregation state of beta-amyloids in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
beta A1-42 is neurotoxic in a cell culture system, but the neurotoxicity is not directly related to its ability to form fibrils.
the neurotoxicity and fibrillization of beta A1 40 are interrelated.
the neurotoxicity is a function of the aggregation state of beta A1 40.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
beta-amyloid fibrils are neurotoxic, and that beta-sheet conformation of the peptide is a prerequisite for fibrillar structure.
fibril formation of beta amyloid peptide is a time dependent process and that the rate of formation is related to the neurotoxicity.
the aggregation of beta A1–40 is a dynamic process that is influenced by many factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a correlation between the degree of fibrillization of the amyloid and neurotoxicity.
the aggregation state of the beta-amyloid protein is an important consideration in the design and interpretation of in vitro and in vivo experiments.
the neurotoxic effects of beta A can be modulated by altering its aggregation state, and that this can be achieved by altering the peptide sequence.
